personal.name: MIRAS Romain
personal.title: Software Engineer & DevOps Specialist
personal.bio:
As a recent computer science graduate from Polytech Grenoble, I am starting my career in DevOps/Backend at Viseo Grenoble and remain open to other permanent contract opportunities in DevOps, Backend, or FullStack.

After completing a 2-year IUT in Informatics at Université Grenoble Alpes (equivalent to a Bachelor's degree), I developed solid foundations in various areas of IT — with a strong focus on Web Development, Software Engineering. I was then able to enroll in the Polytech Grenoble engineering school, which allowed me to strengthen my skills in this field and, more recently, in DevOps.

During my career, I have worked on projects combining backend development (Dotnet, Spring Boot, etc.), DevOps (CI/CD, Docker, GitLab), and sometimes frontend (React). I enjoy exploring the entire lifecycle of an application, from design to production.

I am open to permanent contract opportunities in DevOps, Backend, or FullStack starting in September 2025, in France or internationally.

projects.title: OS Portfolio
projects.description: Immersive portfolio simulating an operating system
projects.longDescription: A unique interactive portfolio that simulates the experience of a custom operating system. Developed with React, TypeScript and TailwindCSS, it offers an innovative user interface with draggable windows, an interactive terminal and smooth animations using Framer Motion.

projects.title: KUIS - Kubernetes Web UI
projects.description: Lightweight web interface for Kubernetes cluster management directly from your browser
projects.longDescription: KUIS (Kubernetes Web UI) is a minimalist and performant Kubernetes management interface, designed as a lightweight alternative to heavy solutions like Kubernetes Dashboard or Lens. The project delivers a complete user experience with a single ~30MB binary including the frontend, directly accessible from any browser. Built with Go and Fiber for the backend and React/TypeScript for the frontend, it enables interactive resource browsing, log streaming, interactive container shell access, real-time YAML editing, and management of multiple kubeconfig files. Positioned as 'K9s for the browser', it combines terminal tool speed with web application accessibility.

projects.title: VTAH: AG-UI Protocol
projects.description: Public technical presentation on the AG-UI Protocol
projects.longDescription: Recorded and publicly shared technical presentation on AG-UI Protocol, a key element of modern agentic systems. I presented in detail the protocol's functionality, architecture, and practical applications with CopilotKit and Microsoft Agent Framework. This presentation aims to educate the tech community about AI agent orchestration protocols and their use cases. Watch the full video via the link above to discover live demos and implementation examples.

projects.title: VTAH: Model Context Protocol
projects.description: Public technical presentation on the Model Context Protocol
projects.longDescription: Recorded and publicly shared technical presentation on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an emerging standard for communication between AI and external tools. I explored in detail how MCP facilitates the integration of tools with modern AI models, its benefits, and practical implementations with GitHub Copilot and other AI assistants. Check out the full video via the link above to see practical demos and understand how to adopt MCP in your projects.

projects.title: Personal Server on Raspberry Pi
projects.description: Installation and management of a self-hosted multifunction server on Raspberry Pi
projects.longDescription: Personal project involving the installation and configuration of a multifunction server on Raspberry Pi. I set up the system (Raspberry Pi OS), installed and maintained several services: web server (Apache with reverse proxy and HTTPS via Let’s Encrypt), file server (Samba), automated backup tools, network monitoring, and hosting of static/dynamic sites accessible locally and remotely.

projects.title: My Best Menus
projects.description: Balanced menu website with CI/CD and automated cloud infrastructure
projects.longDescription: University project carried out by a team of 6, aiming to develop a web platform offering weekly personalized balanced menus according to user preferences. I acted as Lead Developer, leading the technical design, setting up cloud infrastructure on Azure via Terraform, and automating CI/CD deployments. The application was developed with React for the frontend and Spring Boot for the backend, ensuring robustness, scalability, and DevOps best practices.

projects.title: Sea Of Crabes
projects.description: Award-winning Game Jam project: development of an isometric game in native Java with a custom graphics engine.
projects.longDescription: Project completed during a three-week Game Jam at Polytech Grenoble, led by a team of 7 third-year engineering students. I served as project manager and lead developer. We designed a 2D isometric rendering engine in native Java from scratch and developed all game mechanics. This project won first place in the competition, demonstrating our ability to manage a complete development cycle, from technical design to delivering a functional product within tight deadlines.

projects.title: Tech a Way
projects.description: Web project for the development of the Tech A Way client website.
projects.longDescription: Tech a Way is a recruitment agency specialized in the tech sector, operating fully remotely and across Europe. This academic project involved developing a complete web platform in PHP to facilitate the recruitment process, from candidate application to final hiring. The platform features candidate management, job postings, and recruiter dashboards, providing an end-to-end solution for tech recruitment. The project was carried out as a client assignment for 'Tech A Way', with a focus on delivering a robust, user-friendly, and secure recruitment site tailored to the client's needs.
